title: SELLING A PHYSICAL ONE-OFF: MINE OR SOMEONE ELSE'S?
content:
If you want to sell a physical product, the next question is not whether you personally know how to manufacture one. The question is whether you want the product and brand to be yours.

Your product could be something you make with your own hands, something a manufacturer produces for your brand, or something genuinely new that you develop. In each case, you own or control the offer even if other people participate in production.

The other route is to sell a physical product another business owns through resale, dropshipping, or referral.

OWNERSHIP IS ABOUT CONTROL, NOT FACTORY WORK
A trainer can design a shaker's specifications, colors, branding, and packaging while a manufacturer produces every unit. That can still be the trainer's product. Buying another brand's shaker wholesale is a different business relationship even if the objects look similar.

Owning can provide more control over branding, specifications, and long-term strategy, while requiring more development, money, and supplier responsibility. Selling someone else's product can reduce development work while increasing dependence on another company.

EXAMPLE
Own product: You choose a lunch container design, dimensions, materials, branding, and packaging, then hire a manufacturer to produce it for your brand.

Someone else's product: You buy an existing container brand at wholesale and resell it.

The factory may be involved in both examples. The meaningful difference is who controls the product being offered.

I WANT THE PRODUCT/BRAND TO BE MINE → PDF 12.
I WANT TO SELL A PHYSICAL PRODUCT THAT ALREADY BELONGS TO ANOTHER COMPANY → PDF 16.

THE OWNERSHIP QUESTION CHANGES YOUR STARTING WORK

Imagine two people both want to sell insulated water bottles.

One wants a bottle under her own brand with particular dimensions, lid design, colors, packaging, and features. Her early work concerns the product itself: what her version should be, whether an existing manufacturer can make it, minimum quantities, samples, specifications, costs, quality, and the responsibilities that come with putting her product into the market.

The other finds an existing bottle she already likes and wants to earn money selling it. Her early work is different. She needs to understand the possible selling arrangements: buying inventory wholesale, having a supplier dropship orders, or referring customers as an affiliate.

The physical object might even come from the same broader supply chain. What changes is what the business owns and controls.

Owning the product can create more control over differentiation, branding, pricing decisions, and the long-term asset you are building. Selling an existing product can remove much of the development burden but makes you more dependent on another company's product and terms.

WHAT YOU ARE CHOOSING

If you choose MINE, you are volunteering to solve a product development problem. You need to decide what should exist and how it will reliably become a physical product.

If you choose SOMEONE ELSE'S, you are volunteering to solve a selling-arrangement problem. The product already exists, and you need to decide how you want to participate in its sale.

Neither choice tells you how profitable the business will be. It tells you what kind of work comes next.

WHERE TO GO NEXT
If the product itself should belong to your business, continue to PDF 12. If you want to sell products owned by another company, continue to PDF 16.
